hints.title: Tree Poset Extension Formulation
hints.text: The construction constraints define a rooted tree where each child requires its parent to be built first.

hints.title: Subtree Size Hook Formula
hints.text: the number of linear extensions of a tree poset is given by n factorial divided by the product of all subtree sizes.

hints.title: Fermat Modular Inverses
hints.text: compute subtree sizes using postorder traversal, then calculate n factorial multiplied by the modular inverse of the product of subtree sizes using Fermat Little Theorem.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Subtree sizes calculated in post-order; denominator inverted via modular exponentiation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all topological permutations of tree nodes takes factorial time and memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Subtree size counting and modular inverse factorial runs in O(N log MOD) time with O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should know the hook-length theorem or tree topological sort formula N! / prod(subtree_size).
